quests.instruction: A ripe watermelon and a fresh peach both release a lot of liquid with every bite. Which word describes that?
quests.hint: This word describes a fruit that practically drips with every bite.
quests.explanation: That's right! A ripe watermelon and fresh peach both release a lot of liquid with every bite, described as juicy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? juicy fruits are filled with water and incredibly refreshing to eat.

quests.instruction: A quince eaten raw and an unripe banana share this sharp, unsweet flavor. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This taste usually fades away once a fruit is properly ripened or cooked.
quests.explanation: Great job! A quince eaten raw and an unripe banana share this sharp, unsweet flavor, called bitter!
quests.funFact: Did you know? the white part of an orange peel is extremely bitter.

quests.instruction: A bite of rhubarb and a firm green plum both share this crisp, bright flavor. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste feels sharp and lively without being unpleasantly sour.
quests.explanation: You got it! A bite of rhubarb and a firm green plum both share this crisp, bright flavor, called tart!
quests.funFact: Did you know? tart foods make your mouth pucker up because they are so sour.

quests.instruction: Grapes and ripe mangoes both taste this way once they're fully ripened. What word fits?
quests.hint: This taste usually grows stronger the longer a fruit sits in the sun.
quests.explanation: Well done! Grapes and ripe mangoes both taste this way once fully ripened, called sweet!
quests.funFact: Eating sweet fruit is a much healthier dessert than eating candy.

quests.instruction: A ripe peach and a fresh plum both leave your fingers a little sticky and wet. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes fruit that's the opposite of dry and crumbly.
quests.explanation: Correct! A ripe peach and fresh plum both leave fingers sticky and wet, described as juicy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? watermelons and oranges are famously juicy.

quests.instruction: The seeds inside a papaya and citrus pith both carry this sharp, less-sweet flavor. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This taste is one reason certain parts of a fruit are often left uneaten.
quests.explanation: Super! The seeds inside a papaya and citrus pith both carry this sharp, less-sweet flavor, called bitter!
quests.funFact: Did you know? grapefruit has a slightly bitter taste mixed with its sweetness.

quests.instruction: Grapefruit pith and unripe olives both carry this same sharp, unsweet flavor. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This taste is why olives need special preparation before they're ready to eat.
quests.explanation: Nice work! Grapefruit pith and unripe olives both carry this same sharp, unsweet flavor, called bitter!
quests.funFact: Did you know? humans evolved to detect bitter tastes to avoid poisonous plants.

quests.instruction: A ripe orange and a fresh plum both squirt liquid when you bite into them. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes a fruit you might need a napkin for.
quests.explanation: You found it! A ripe orange and fresh plum both squirt liquid when bitten into, described as juicy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? a really juicy fruit will drip down your chin when you bite it.

quests.instruction: A crisp Asian pear and a firm apple both make this same loud, snapping sound when bitten. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes a bite you can practically hear across the room.
quests.explanation: Exactly right! A crisp Asian pear and firm apple both make this loud, snapping sound when bitten, described as crunchy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? crunchy fruits are great for your teeth and jaw muscles.

quests.instruction: A slice of grapefruit and a fresh pineapple wedge share this lively, zesty flavor. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes a taste with a fun kick, not overwhelmingly sour.
quests.explanation: Wonderful! A slice of grapefruit and fresh pineapple wedge share this lively, zesty flavor, called tangy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? tangy flavors make your tongue tingle.

quests.instruction: Ripe mangoes and watermelon both have a sugary taste kids love. Which word describes that taste?
quests.hint: This is the taste that makes a fruit perfect for dessert.
quests.explanation: Terrific! Ripe mangoes and watermelon both have that sugary taste, which is called sweet!
quests.funFact: Did you know? sweetness in fruit comes from natural sugars.

quests.instruction: An unripe green mango and a tart cranberry share a sharp bite. What's that taste called?
quests.hint: This taste often shows up before a fruit is fully ripe.
quests.explanation: Yes! An unripe green mango and tart cranberry share that sharp bite called sour!
quests.funFact: Did you know? adding sugar to sour lemon juice makes delicious lemonade.

quests.instruction: A firm nashi pear and a crisp green apple share this same satisfying snap. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This word describes a fruit's texture, from its very first bite.
quests.explanation: That's right! A firm nashi pear and crisp green apple share this same satisfying snap, described as crunchy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? keeping fruits cold in the fridge helps them stay crunchy longer.

quests.instruction: A ripe tomato and a watermelon slice both squirt liquid everywhere when bitten. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This word describes a fruit that might dribble down your chin.
quests.explanation: Great job! A ripe tomato and watermelon slice both squirt liquid when bitten, described as juicy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? juicy fruits are the best choice for making fresh squeezed drinks.

quests.instruction: A juicy peach and a ripe pear both have this sugary flavor. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This is the taste most kids ask for a second helping of.
quests.explanation: You got it! A juicy peach and ripe pear both have this sugary flavor, called sweet!
quests.funFact: Did you know? our bodies naturally crave sweet fruits because they provide quick energy.

quests.instruction: Fresh cranberries and unripe grapes both share this same puckering taste. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This is the taste candy makers sometimes copy on purpose for a fun snack.
quests.explanation: Well done! Fresh cranberries and unripe grapes both share that same puckering taste called sour!
quests.funFact: Did you know? eating sour candy mimics the taste of very sour fruit.

quests.instruction: Strawberries and cherries share this sugary taste when they're fully ripe. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste is the opposite of the one that makes your face pucker.
quests.explanation: Correct! Strawberries and cherries share this sugary taste when ripe, called sweet!
quests.funFact: Did you know? pineapples and mangoes are incredibly sweet when they are fully ripe.

quests.instruction: A firm green apple and a fresh gooseberry pie share this crisp, tangy flavor. What's the word?
quests.hint: This is the pleasant sharpness bakers love using in a good fruit pie.
quests.explanation: Super! A firm green apple and fresh gooseberry pie share this crisp, tangy flavor, called tart!
quests.funFact: Did you know? cranberries are famous for being incredibly tart.

quests.instruction: A ripe pear and a fresh grape both burst with liquid in a single bite. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word is the opposite of a dry, crumbly texture.
quests.explanation: Nice work! A ripe pear and fresh grape both burst with liquid in one bite, described as juicy!
quests.funFact: Fun fact: juicy fruits are filled with water and incredibly refreshing to eat.

quests.instruction: Underripe blueberries and fresh currants both have this pleasantly sharp bite. What's the word?
quests.hint: This word describes a taste that's sharp in a pleasant, not overwhelming, way.
quests.explanation: You found it! Underripe blueberries and fresh currants both have this pleasantly sharp bite, called tart!
quests.funFact: Did you know? bakers often add lots of sugar to tart fruits to make them taste better.

quests.instruction: A ripe pineapple and a fresh tangerine share a zesty, slightly sharp flavor along with their sweetness. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This word describes a taste that's sweet with a lively, zesty kick.
quests.explanation: Exactly right! A ripe pineapple and fresh tangerine share this zesty, slightly sharp flavor, called tangy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? yogurt often has a slightly tangy taste from healthy bacteria.

quests.instruction: A firm, unripe mango and a crisp green apple share this same snappy bite. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This word describes texture, not the sweet or sour taste of a fruit.
quests.explanation: Wonderful! A firm, unripe mango and crisp green apple share this same snappy bite, described as crunchy!
quests.funFact: Fun fact: crunchy fruits make a loud snapping sound when you bite into them.

quests.instruction: An overripe mango and a very soft, overripe strawberry share this same squishy texture. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This word describes fruit texture on the far side of perfectly ripe.
quests.explanation: Terrific! An overripe mango and very soft, overripe strawberry share this same squishy texture, described as mushy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? overripe bananas get mushy and are perfect for baking bread.

quests.instruction: Fresh cranberries and slightly underripe grapes share this brisk, pleasant flavor. Which word matches?
quests.hint: This taste sits right between plain sour and fully sweet.
quests.explanation: Yes! Fresh cranberries and slightly underripe grapes share this brisk, pleasant flavor, called tart!
quests.funFact: Did you know? a tart green apple is perfect for baking a pie.

quests.instruction: An overripe banana with brown spots and a very soft, overripe peach both squish easily when pressed. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This word describes a texture that gives way easily under gentle pressure.
quests.explanation: That's right! An overripe banana with brown spots and a very soft, overripe peach both squish easily, described as mushy!
quests.funFact: Did you know? mushy fruit is very easy for babies to eat.

quests.instruction: Ripe bananas and grapes share the same sugary taste. What's that taste called?
quests.hint: This taste often gets stronger the riper a fruit becomes.
quests.explanation: Great job! Ripe bananas and grapes share that same sugary taste, called sweet!
quests.funFact: Did you know? eating sweet fruit is a much healthier dessert than eating candy.

quests.instruction: The rind of a watermelon and an unripe persimmon both share this sharp, less-pleasant taste. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste is the reason some fruit parts get peeled away or left uneaten.
quests.explanation: You got it! The rind of a watermelon and an unripe persimmon both share this sharp, less-pleasant taste, called bitter!
quests.funFact: Fun fact: bitter is a sharp taste that many people have to learn to like.

quests.instruction: A firm green apple and an unripe pear both have this same satisfying, snappy texture. Which word fits?
quests.hint: This word describes the opposite texture of a soft, overripe banana.
quests.explanation: Well done! A firm green apple and unripe pear both have this same satisfying, snappy texture, described as crunchy!
quests.funFact: Fun fact: a fresh apple is famously crunchy and crisp.

quests.instruction: A slice of lemon and an underripe plum share a sharp, puckery taste. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste can make your whole face scrunch up.
quests.explanation: Correct! A slice of lemon and underripe plum share that sharp, puckery taste called sour!
quests.funFact: Fun fact: sour fruits have a high level of acidity that makes your mouth pucker.

quests.instruction: A ripe orange and a fresh lychee both share this zesty flavor along with their sweetness. What's the word?
quests.hint: This taste has a little zip to it, more lively than plain sweet.
quests.explanation: Super! A ripe orange and fresh lychee both share this zesty flavor, called tangy!
quests.funFact: Fun fact: a tangy flavor is a sharp, strong taste that wakes up your mouth.
